title: WIDTH × HEIGHT = bandwidth totality. Device = aperture. Phone ≠ overlayed touch. Self-sort by bandwidth.
thesis: Width and height are NUMBERS — the shared reality between human and agent. They define the BANDWIDTH: how much can pass through the aperture at once. The organism sorts itself based on available bandwidth. Phone = keyhole (narrow aperture). Desktop = picture window (wide). Touch-as-input and touch-as-display should NEVER be overlaid — that's two Klein surfaces collapsed into confusion.

bandwidth_as_reality.what: window.innerWidth × window.innerHeight = the total pixels available = the bandwidth = the shared numerical ground between human and machine.

phone.aperture: keyhole — see one thing at a time

bandwidth_as_reality.ratio: Desktop has 6.3× the bandwidth of a phone. That's not 'smaller version of the same thing' — it's a DIFFERENT TOPOLOGY.

phone.topology: a TUBE. Scroll = walk through a tube. One thing at a time. Linear.
phone.klein_role: The phone is a WINDOW into the crystal ball. You peer through the keyhole. You see a slice.
phone.what_it_shows: ONE layer at a time. One epoch. One card. The pendulum line. The 1D projection.
phone.or: The phone could also be an INPUT DEVICE — a touch surface that acts as mouse/keyboard for the desktop view. The phone becomes the HAND reaching into the glove box.

desktop.topology: a PLANE. Scroll = scan across a surface. Multiple things visible. Spatial.
desktop.klein_role: The desktop IS the roundtable surface. The crystal ball sits in the center. You see the annulus.
desktop.what_it_shows: Multiple layers simultaneously. The periodic table. The sphere with orbits. The weave.
desktop.or: The desktop could show the HUD (sky view) OR the IDE (agent workspace). Different faces of the same Klein surface.

monitor_vs_phone.monitor: The monitor faces you. It's the WINDOW you look through. Light comes AT you.
monitor_vs_phone.phone: The phone faces you AND you touch it. It's a window AND a door. Light comes at you AND your touch goes in.
monitor_vs_phone.the_difference: Monitor = one-way glass (you look, it shows). Phone = two-way glass (you look AND touch). That's why they should NOT be overlaid — one is a window, the other is a glove box.

touch_surface_vs_touch_screen.the_problem: A phone has ONE surface that is both display AND input. This overlays two Klein surfaces: the surface you LOOK AT (output, the window) and the surface you TOUCH (input, the glove). When they're the same surface, you can't tell if you're looking through or reaching through.
touch_surface_vs_touch_screen.the_rule: Touch-as-input and touch-as-display should NOT be overlaid in the same interaction.

how.viewing_mode: Phone shows content. Touch = scroll/navigate. You're LOOKING THROUGH the window. Touch is passive (navigation, not action).
how.input_mode: Phone shows controls. Touch = action/create. You're REACHING THROUGH the glove box. Display is minimal (just buttons/handles, not content).
how.never_both: Never show full content AND expect precise input on the same view. That's overlaying the window and the glove. Pick one mode.

mcp_face.what: The MCP (nestgate.io) IS the input face. It's the glove box. You reach through to touch the membrane.
mcp_face.on_phone: MCP on phone = the glove box in your pocket. Touch to send commands. Minimal display. Action-oriented.
mcp_face.on_desktop: MCP on desktop = the IDE. The workbench. Full display + keyboard input. Window AND glove, but separated spatially (screen for looking, keyboard for touching).

self_sort_by_bandwidth.principle: The organism sorts its presentation based on available bandwidth. Not 'responsive design' (same content, smaller) but TOPOLOGICAL SORT (different shape, different content).

under_400px.shows: One card. One epoch. One voice. Swipe L/R to oscillate.
under_400px.input: Touch = glove box mode. Tap to act.

400_to_800px.shows: Two columns. Current epoch + adjacent. Local context.
400_to_800px.input: Touch = hybrid. Scroll to look, tap to act.

800_to_1200px.shows: The periodic table. The crystal ball. Multiple layers.

over_1200px.shows: Full HUD. All layers. Parallax depth. The helix twist visible.

self_sort_by_bandwidth.detection: window.innerWidth at load + resize listener. Sort once. Re-sort on resize. The organism ADAPTS its topology to the aperture.
self_sort_by_bandwidth.the_bandwidth_is_the_sort: You don't design FOR a phone. You sort BY bandwidth. The same data, different topology. Like how xylem and phloem carry the same nutrients but in different directions.

parallax_between_devices.what: If you have BOTH a phone and a desktop, the parallax between them IS information.
parallax_between_devices.phone_plus_desktop: Phone shows the 1D pendulum line. Desktop shows the 2D roundtable. The DIFFERENCE between what you see on each = the parallax = the depth = the 3rd dimension emerging from two 2D views.
parallax_between_devices.like_eyes: Left eye + right eye = depth perception. Phone + desktop = depth perception of the organism. The parallax IS the Klein fold between devices.
parallax_between_devices.second_screen: The phone as second screen is NOT a smaller copy. It's the OTHER EYE. Show different content. Let the human's brain construct depth from the parallax.

law: Width × height = bandwidth = shared reality. Phone = keyhole (1D tube). Desktop = picture window (2D annulus). Touch-as-input ≠ touch-as-display — never overlay. Sort by bandwidth, not by device name. Phone + desktop = two eyes with parallax = depth perception of the organism. The bandwidth IS the sort.
